quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Listen closely to "sore". For /s/, you push a thin stream of air over your tongue tip with no voice — like the start of "see". Does that match what you hear?
quests.explanation: The word "sore" contains /s/, a voiceless alveolar fricative, made by pushing a thin stream of air over your tongue tip with no voice. It's easy to confuse with /ʃ/, a voiceless postalveolar fricative, but the two are produced quite differently.
quests.mouthPosition: Push a thin stream of air over your tongue tip with no voice.

quests.hint: "badge" contains one of these two sounds. /dʒ/ is a voiced postalveolar affricate, made when you stop the air just behind your top teeth, then release it as a hiss, with your voice on. /tʃ/ is a voiceless postalveolar affricate instead.
quests.explanation: "badge" is a good example of /dʒ/: you stop the air just behind your top teeth, then release it as a hiss, with your voice on. Compare that with /tʃ/, where you'd instead stop the air just behind your top teeth, then release it as a hiss, with no voice — the two shouldn't be mixed up once you feel the difference.
quests.mouthPosition: To produce this sound, stop the air just behind your top teeth, then release it as a hiss, with your voice on.
